title: Comparative efficacy of tool-augmentation versus constrained decoding for preventing high-risk semantic misconfigurations under adversarial intents (repaired/preregistered)
research_question: Under adversarial or out-of-distribution intent prompts, does tool-augmentation (generate→validate→repair) reduce high-risk semantic misconfigurations relative to LLM-only generation in vendor-specific intent→configuration pipelines?
confirmatory_hypotheses: H1: Tool-augmented pipelines (generate→validate→repair) produce a lower high-risk semantic failure rate than LLM-only generation (paired comparison).

H2: The absolute reduction in high-risk semantic failure rate between tool-augmented and LLM-only pipelines is at least 5 percentage points (the primary minimum-detectable-effect used for sample-size justification).
exploratory_questions: E1: How do failure-mode frequencies (ACL, routing, interface/address overlap, BGP/neighbor misconfig) differ between pipelines?
E2: Does constrained/grammar-aware decoding (not available as a confirmatory adapter) offer complementary benefits when combined with tool-augmentation? (exploratory descriptive analyses only)
benchmark_scope: Public vendor-configuration corpora and intent→configuration pairs derived only from redistributable public datasets referenced in the supplied evidence records (see evidence_record_ids).
Adversarial intent set used for stress-testing is algorithmically generated; potentially sensitive exemplars will be redacted on public release per the contamination plan.
primary_estimand: Paired absolute difference in high-risk semantic failure proportions (LLM-only minus tool-augmented) across the predeclared task sample, computed by the paired_binary_analysis_v1 executor.
secondary_estimands: Per-vendor paired absolute differences (Cisco IOS, Juniper Junos).
Repair success rate: proportion of initial-validator-failed tasks where a single automated repair produces a validator-pass.
Failure-mode relative-frequency differences by category (ACL, routing, neighbor, interface/address).
sampling_plan: Confirmatory paired design using the hosted_netops_gvr_v1 adapter. task_count = 600 paired tasks selected deterministically via the adapter's challenging_workflow_stress_v1 index rule (selection is outcome-independent and fixed before any model calls). Episodes_per_task = 2 (baseline and guarded). Per adapter contract: one shared initial generation per task (used unchanged across paired conditions) and at most one guarded repair call if the deterministic validator fails. Runtime sampling parameters (temperature, top_p, other runtime generation parameters) will be recorded for every model call; no claim of deterministic sampling is made.
power_and_precision_plan: Primary power target: detect an absolute difference of 5 percentage points with ≈80% power at α=0.05 under conservative paired-difference approximations. Assumptions: baseline semantic high-risk failure rate ≈10%, two-sided α=0.05, paired design. N=600 pairs provides ≈80% power to detect a 5 percentage-point absolute difference under these assumptions. Sensitivity analyses will recompute power/CI under baseline rates 5% and 15% and will report bootstrap CIs for the primary estimand.
exclusion_rules: Exclude any dataset item lacking a public-source URL and license tag (flagged by automated provenance check).
Exclude confirmatory-sample items flagged by automated consistency checks (ambiguous ground-truth configurations) after additional automatic checks.
Exclude items redacted for safety (adversarial examples with exploit payloads) from the primary confirmatory analysis; counts and reasons reported.
missingness_plan: Primary analysis treatment: 'complete_pair_primary' — pairs with technical infrastructure/model-call failures are excluded from the confirmatory test and reported with counts and reasons. A sensitivity analysis ('complete_pair_primary_with_failure_as_zero_sensitivity') will treat technical failures as semantic failures. All model-call failures (initial generation vs. repair attempt) and adapter errors will be logged with timestamps and locations.
analysis_plan: Primary analysis executed by paired_binary_analysis_v1: McNemar-style paired comparison of binary final semantic-pass outcomes (validator pass/fail) between baseline and guarded conditions, reporting absolute risk difference and two-sided 95% CIs (as provided by the executor). Secondary analyses: vendor-stratified paired estimates, Fisher-exact tests for failure-mode frequency differences with Bonferroni correction across secondary test family, bootstrap CIs for repair success rates, and sensitivity analyses treating technical failures as failures. All analyses will use the paired_binary_analysis_v1 executor and its supported failed_call_treatment options. Runtime sampling parameters and full raw outputs will be archived and hashed for reproducibility.
multiplicity_plan: Primary hypothesis (H1/H2) is the single confirmatory test. Secondary tests are labeled exploratory; reported p-values for secondary confirmatory-family tests will be Bonferroni-corrected across the declared family. No multiplicity correction applied to purely exploratory descriptive charts; all exploratory inferences explicitly labeled as exploratory.
contamination_plan: Dataset provenance checks and automated redaction: (1) require public-source URL and license for inclusion in confirmatory sample; (2) hash-based duplication detection vs archived pre-lock artifacts to prevent reuse of pre-lock development payloads; (3) algorithmic redaction of adversarial examples containing exploit substrings before public release (full hashed artifacts retained privately); (4) flagged items (missing license, exploit patterns, ambiguous ground-truth) are excluded from the confirmatory primary analysis and reported with counts and rationales. Sensitivity analyses will report confirmatory results with and without flagged items where safe redactions permit.
stopping_rule: Stop when all predeclared task_indices are processed or when the adapter's maximum_model_calls (task_count * 2 = 1200) are exhausted. No interim outcome-dependent stopping or sample-size peeking is permitted.
planned_outputs: Preregistered experiment plan (this document) with hashes and adapter-contract metadata.
